items.title: Germaine Bazzle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006
items.q: If you can see the Humphrey Brothers and all of these guys over here in Preservation Hall

ctx.x: Let me answer that this way. I became aware of it because of some things that happened in New Orleans, the Mardi Gras. Okay? My parents were in a marching club. So at Mardi Gras they dressed in these costumes and had the band and they marched around. And I grew up with that. And it was understood that this is a part of you, this is a part of what we do, you know, you don’t have to embrace it but you have to be aware of it. Then being around, living in a neighborhood where there were many musicians and you’d hear…

kitchen table and tapping and looking and seeing my father peek around the door. You know and I’m sharing all of these little things with you because that’s how much music was in my life or is in my life now. And as I got older I moved into an area called like the Tremé area of our city where a lot of the music is and where it really came from. You know we have these second lines and the parades and all of this and the people are dancing in the street and all, and then I had the opportunity to go to Preservation…

No, no, no. You said that very well. My wife and I were in New Orleans just about a year ago. And we were walking I think on Canal Street I guess, and we could hear this sound of this band and we literally followed the sound. And then on the corner of I guess Bourbon Street there was this group of young kids playing. And they were unbelievable. You couldn’t possibly write down what they were playing. And I just thought that was a joy to see, that that still goes on. Is there any organization to that kind of…
